text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The former ruling Party of Social Democracy opposes cuts in subsidies for the mining sector.
- The government decided to control the State Ownership Fund privatisation body.
- The government decided to cut import taxes for farm products.
- A court in the Transylvanian city of Brasov ruled that the Caritas SRL company, which launched a pyramid investment scheme in 1992 and syphoned the savings of millions of Romanians, was banckrupt.
- The government suggested the privatisation of Petromidia SA oil refinery and gave up initial plans to close down the loss-making refinery.
- The Senate passed bill on bank privatisation.
- The Darmanesti SA oil refinery, put by the government on a list of loss-making firms earmarked for closure, might be privatised, the paper says.
- A consortium led by Canada's Telesystem International Wireless launched Romania's first GSM mobile telephone system.
- Regia Radiocomunicatii RA radio authority might halt broadcasts of the state radio and television following their alleged failure to pay old debts, the paper says.
